Mia Chen: Heads-up — observed out-of-phase tokens after an epoch rotation on prod-3. Memory climbs steadily after ~25k tokens and we see stale KV pages being reused across different requests.
Lucas Patel: Can you paste the logs and a short repro?
Mia Chen: Minimal log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] kvcache: alloc bucket=7 offset=4096 epoch=1024 req=abcd
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] kvcache: append chunk offset=2048 tag=0x1 req=efgh
[2026-03-17T14:05:13Z] kvcache: lookup bucket=7 offset=4096 epoch=1025 req=ijkl -> TAG_MISMATCH
[2026-03-17T14:05:13Z] kvcache: evict tombstone bucket=7 epoch=1024
```
Seems like epoch increments but bucket offsets/tags aren't consistently updated, so lookups hit stale pages. Repro locally with long-context harness (seq ~60k) + prefetched kv pages + concurrent requests.
DevBot: perf-regression-alert: kvcache-miss-rate spike 3.2x at 14:06 (pid=3124)
Natasha Iyer: Steps to reproduce?
Mia Chen: Short repro: run long-chat-load test with kv-prefetch=true, send 3 concurrent request_ids while forcing an epoch rollover (sleep and trigger compaction). After rollover, request B occasionally reads a page written by request A (different request_id) -> wrong token outputs.
Lucas Patel: Hypothesis: bucket index uses (epoch ^ request_id) in lookup, but the eviction/append path computes a fingerprint that drops high bits of epoch due to packing/quantization. That asymmetric encoding would yield stale hits if epoch wraps/truncates.
Omar Ruiz: Profiling shows a memcpy hotspot in the eviction path around page compaction. Flamegraph: https://internal/fg/2332 (staging). Also see memory growth trace attached.
Mia Chen: Stack trace snippet: 
```
kvcache::lookup
kvcache::resolve_tag
kvcache::evict_compact
memcpy
```
Lucas Patel: Fix idea: include full epoch in the page fingerprint/tombstone checks (don't truncate to 16 bits). Also add a checksum that includes request_id. That should prevent reuse across epoch boundaries. Need to evaluate footprint impact.
Natasha Iyer: Add unit test simulating: epoch rollover + concurrent writes + immediate lookups. Also add a fuzz that flips epoch at random times to catch races.
Mia Chen: I drafted a patch and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 — adds epoch to fingerprint + new tombstone writer + test harness.
DevBot: CI: running (infra-ci) -> smoke tests queued.
Omar Ruiz: Quick perf note: early staging run shows ~1.4% p50 increase on small batches with epoch-in-fingerprint enabled, but eliminates cross-request contamination and reduces long-context memory growth. Full perf run scheduled.
Lucas Patel: Let's gate behind a runtime flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in after testing. If perf cost is acceptable we flip later. Also we should add a compacting background job to clear stale pages quicker to mitigate mem growth.
Mia Chen: Assigning @Lucas Patel for code review and @Omar Ruiz for perf validation. I will push an additional end-to-end test that simulates heavy concurrent long contexts.
Natasha Iyer: I'll add this to the postmortem/regression bucket and track follow-ups.
Mia Chen: :thumbsup: Thanks all, will update when staging perf run completes.
DevBot: Note: PR merged to staging branch after review; marking thread for tracking.
